In 4-dimensional [[geometry]], the '''tetrahedral cupola''' is a [[polychoron]] bounded by one [[tetrahedron]], a parallel [[cuboctahedron]], connected by 10 [[triangular prism]]s, and 4 [[triangular pyramid]]s.<ref>[http://www.bendwavy.org/klitzing/pdf/artConvSeg_8.pdf Convex Segmentochora] Dr. Richard Klitzing, Symmetry: Culture and Science, Vol. 11, Nos. 1-4, 139-181, 2000 (4.23 tetrahedron || cuboctahedron)</ref>

== Related polytopes==
The ''tetrahedral cupola'' can be sliced off from a [[runcinated 5-cell]], on a [[hyperplane]] parallel to a tetrahedral cell. The [[cuboctahedron]] base passes through the center of the runcinated 5-cell, so the Tetrahedral cupola contains half of the tetrahedron and triangular prism cells of the runcinated 5-cell. The cupola can be seen in A<sub>2</sub> and A<sub>3</sub> Coxeter plane orthogonal projection of the runcinated 5-cell:
